headline: Tennessee Senator Marsha Blackburn, running for governor, was mocked for posting an AI video of herself and other Republicans dancing to a song by US rapper Kendrick Lamar.
score_reason: Funny and widely shared political cringe; limited consequence. Posted 13 Oct, so slightly dated.
importance_line: It shows AI video entering a US governor's race as early voting opens and drawing ridicule, including from the Democratic nominee; there is no policy effect and the video's origin is disputed in detail.
source: The National News Desk, relaying Mediaite
summary: The National News Desk reports, relaying Mediaite, that US Senator Marsha Blackburn, 74, a Republican running for governor of Tennessee, posted a 12-second AI video on X on 13 Oct 2026 of herself and fellow Tennessee Republicans dancing to 'Not Like Us' by US rapper Kendrick Lamar, and critics including Democratic nominee Jerri Green called it embarrassing. Blackburn told WZTV that a county commissioner made the video and called it 'a funsie'.
notes: AL.com page blocked; read the same story as syndicated by WJLA/KATU. url is the page where the text was read. Event 13 Oct, one day before window start; score not lowered because reaction continued on 14 Oct.
